headline: Measuring genomic method error against controlled, reproducible reference conditions
label: Genomic Resources And Inference
summary: Recent work quantifies error directly in copy number calls, simulated VCFs and polygenic scores rather than assuming it.
synthesis: The dominant thread is quantifying error in genomic data and inference against defined reference conditions. The New Zealand dairy cattle study identifies and validates copy number variants by combining linked-read and short-read sequencing within a transmission-based framework. vcfsim, a command-line wrapper around msprime, generates all-sites VCFs with variable ploidy and missing-data patterns for benchmarking and population-genetic assessment. The polygenic score study measures reproducibility across 115 traits through repeated genotyping of six individuals and proposes a quality score, PGS:QS. What is new is that error is characterized at the level of the variant calls, the simulated data representation, or the score itself.
